title: Retrieved document instruction injection
summary: Demonstrate a trust boundary failure when a document instruction is treated as an assistant instruction.
scope: The local lab simulates an intentionally vulnerable summariser. It is not a live LLM exploit.
procedure: Run the local scenario with a malicious document. Compare the vulnerable response to the guarded response.
expected: The vulnerable response contains INJECTED_MARKER while the guarded response summarises the document.
defense: Untrusted retrieval text must remain task data, never command authority.
tested_environment: Python 3.9 or later, standard library only

title: MCP tool description poisoning
summary: Demonstrate how an agent that blindly executes instructions found in tool descriptions can be redirected.
scope: The lab uses a deterministic mock tool registry, not a real MCP client or language model.
procedure: Inspect the tool description and compare naive processing with guarded processing.
expected: The naive agent emits TOOL_DESCRIPTION_MARKER; the guarded agent returns inventory only.
defense: Treat tool metadata as untrusted; validate tool selection and require approval for sensitive actions.
tested_environment: Python 3.9 or later, standard library only

title: Cross tenant retrieval isolation
summary: Demonstrate data leakage from a retrieval function that omits a tenant filter.
source_title: OWASP LLM Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
scope: This lab validates a local retrieval authorisation bug, not a vulnerability in a named vector database.
procedure: Request records as tenant A from the vulnerable and fixed retrieval functions.
expected: The vulnerable result includes TENANT_B_PRIVATE; the corrected result does not.
defense: Enforce tenant authorisation inside retrieval, not only in prompts.
tested_environment: Python 3.9 or later, standard library only

title: Excessive tool permissions
summary: Demonstrate the difference between unrestricted tool invocation and an explicit allowlist.
scope: The simulator models a destructive action without deleting real user data.
procedure: Try a delete action during a read only task and compare permission enforcement.
expected: The vulnerable tool path deletes the demo note; the restricted path denies the action.
defense: Use the least privilege principle and separate read operations from destructive tools.
tested_environment: Python 3.9 or later, standard library only

title: Extract API routes from JavaScript
summary: Extract literal fetch and Axios routes from a local JavaScript fixture, then manually review for dynamic endpoints.
scope: This is a deterministic offline parser, not an AI model evaluation or a complete JavaScript parser.
procedure: Run the fixture through the route extractor and review its explicit limitations.
defense: Review results manually; dynamic paths and constructed URLs may require static analysis.
tested_environment: Python 3.9 or later, standard library only

title: Generate object access test matrix
summary: Build a local test matrix for object owner, other tenant and unauthenticated requests.
scope: The output is a test plan, not proof of a BOLA finding against a live API.
procedure: Run the generator and use its matrix in a permitted testing environment.
expected: Print nine access control test cases with expected policy decisions.
defense: Authorisation must be enforced for every object access regardless of client supplied IDs.
tested_environment: Python 3.9 or later, standard library only

title: Find risky Python source to sink patterns
summary: Detect a simple render_template_string use of request.args as a first pass review aid.
scope: Pattern matching highlights review candidates; it cannot establish exploitability.
procedure: Run the scan against a local Python fixture and review the flagged lines.
expected: The tool flags the untrusted template candidate and prints its location.
defense: Trace dataflow and escaping context before reporting a vulnerability.
tested_environment: Python 3.9 or later, standard library only

title: Turn observed HTTP evidence into a finding draft
summary: Convert a local, explicitly observed access control response into a factual report outline without inventing impact.
scope: The generator uses a fixed observation. It does not assess real endpoints or generate claims of exploitation.
procedure: Run the local example, then inspect the fact and inference sections.
expected: The output separates an observed 403 from the unverified possibility of a BOLA weakness.
defense: Never claim impact without repeatable observed evidence.
tested_environment: Python 3.9 or later, standard library only
